title: The Royal Tiger in the Council Hall (HI)
summary: Panic erupts in the palace when a sentry reports a wild tiger loose in the corridors. Birbal investigates and finds an ordinary stray dog and a shadow.
full_text:
One stormy night in the palace of Agra, an imperial sentry came running into the Diwan-i-Khas, gasping for breath, dropping his spear, and screaming in hysterics: 'A monster! A royal Bengal tiger has slipped past the river gates! I saw its glowing yellow eyes, its striped coat, and its giant claws creeping down the eastern corridor!'

Panic erupted in the council hall! Ministers scrambled behind pillars, generals drew their scimitars, and guards bolted the heavy brass doors, terrified that a man-eating tiger was prowling the palace.

Akbar ordered fifty armed musketeers assembled to storm the corridor.

Birbal stepped forward calmly, picking up a heavy bronze lantern: 'Sire, let us not fire muskets into our own palace halls in blind panic. Allow me to look down the corridor first.'

Birbal walked to the eastern corridor door, opened it a crack, and held his lantern high.

Down the long, drafty hallway, illuminated by the flickering torchlight, a bizarre shadow danced against the whitewashed wall—a towering, monstrous striped shape with glowing eyes and pacing legs!

The guards began to tremble, but Birbal looked not at the wall, but at the floor.

Trotting along the hallway, shivering and whimpering from the cold rain, was an ordinary, wet stray street dog!

The dog was trotting past an iron-grilled window where the moonlight shone through the diagonal wooden slats, casting alternating stripes of black shadow and silver light across the dog's wet fur!

And as the small dog walked past a low oil lamp sitting on the floor, its shadow was magnified twenty times upon the wall, creating the illusion of a giant pacing tiger!

Birbal whistled softly. The frightened little dog wagged its tail, trotted happily up to Birbal, and licked his hand!

Birbal picked up the wet dog in his arms, walked back into the Diwan-i-Khas, and placed the animal upon the council table before the terrified generals and the Emperor:

'Behold, Your Majesty! The ferocious man-eating tiger of the eastern corridor!'

The courtiers gasped, then burst into sheepish, roaring laughter!

Birbal smiled: 'Sire, fear is a magnifying glass that turns a wet puppy into a royal tiger, and a shadow into a demon. When panic shouts, wisdom must light a lamp and look at reality with steady eyes.'

Akbar laughed until his sides ached, rewarded Birbal, and adopted the stray dog as a palace pet.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
